newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher on real-name news.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher on real-name news.

text.p: Stocks closed slightly higher on Thursday after late profit-taking eroded much earlier gains, hich had been sparked by news of possible amendments to the real-name financial system, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed 3.21 points higher at 678.11. It touched a high of 685.95.

"News the government may review the real-name financial regulations improved sentiment. But profit taking emerged because of weak fundamentals," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities. The real-name system bans the use of false names in all financial transactions.

Brokers said the news raised hopes that blackmarket funds would flow into the stock market if restictions were eased. Incoming Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik told reporters he would review ways of improving the real-name system, which is widely believed to have caused bottlenecks in the economy. Brokers estimated there was 17 trillion won circulating in the underground market.

The Bank of Korea's release of February money supply figures had little impact on the market. The bank said money supply measured in M2 rose 19.6 percent in February on the year, compared with a 14.8 percent rise a year earlier.
Construction shares soared on news that the government would offer tax breaks to infrastructure contractors.
The construction sub-index rose 5.86 percent to 302.16.
The ministry said the corporate tax rate for infrastructure contractors would be lowered by three percentage points to 25 percent.
Shares in Dainong Corp and Midopa Department Store went limit down on the news that Shindongbang was considering launching a hostile takeover bid.
Dainong's shares fell 800 won to 10,100, while Midopa lost 3,600 won to 41,500.
Shindongbang's shares were halted for trading by the stock exchange until Saturday. They last traded at 43,500 won.
